question: What is the minimum age to apply for PMEGP?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) — Eligibility rules
- Any individual above 18 years of age can apply.
- There is no income limit.
- For projects costing above Rs 10 lakh in manufacturing, or above Rs 5 lakh in business/service, you must have passed at least Class VIII (8th standard).
- Help is only for new projects sanctioned specifically under PMEGP.
- Only one person per family can get help to set up a project; family means self and spouse.
- For an upgradation (second) loan: the first PMEGP, REGP or MUDRA loan must have been repaid on time, the earlier subsidy adjusted after the 3-year lock-in, and the unit must be making a profit.
Not eligible:
- Existing units set up under PMRY, REGP or any other central or state government scheme cannot apply for a new-unit subsidy.
- Units that have already received a government subsidy under any other central or state scheme are not eligible.
- Projects with no capital expenditure are not financed.
- Activities on the scheme's negative list, or banned by local authorities, are not allowed.
- The cost of land cannot be counted in the project cost.

Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) — How to apply
- Apply online only, on the PMEGP portal run by KVIC; paper applications are not accepted.
- Aadhaar is mandatory and is checked with UIDAI when you file the application.
- The implementing agency (KVIC, State Khadi and Village Industries Board or District Industries Centre) checks the application and sends it to the bank you choose.
- You must complete Entrepreneurship Development Programme (EDP) training before the bank releases the loan, unless you already did at least 10 days (offline) or 60 hours (online) of EDP or skill training.

Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) — Benefits
- Margin money subsidy for General category: 15% of project cost in urban areas and 25% in rural areas.
- Special category (SC, ST, OBC, minorities, women, ex-servicemen, transgender persons, persons with disabilities, North-East region, Aspirational Districts, hill and border areas): 25% in urban areas and 35% in rural areas.
- Your own contribution is 10% of the project cost for General category and 5% for Special category; the bank lends the rest.
- Subsidy applies to project cost up to Rs 50 lakh for manufacturing and Rs 20 lakh for business/service units; banks may lend above this without subsidy.
- A second loan to upgrade an existing PMEGP, REGP or MUDRA unit gets 15% subsidy (20% in North-East and hill states), up to Rs 15 lakh for manufacturing (project up to Rs 1 crore) and Rs 3.75 lakh for service (project up to Rs 25 lakh), or Rs 20 lakh and Rs 5 lakh in North-East and hill states.
- Banks do not ask for collateral on loans up to Rs 20 lakh; the bank charges its normal interest rate, and the subsidy is kept in the beneficiary's name for 3 years before being adjusted.

question: How much premium does a farmer pay for a Kharif crop under PM Fasal Bima Yojana?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Any farmer growing a notified crop in a notified area can be insured, including tenant farmers and sharecroppers.
- The farmer must have an insurable interest in the crop and land, shown by land records (such as RoR or LPC) or a tenancy or sharecropping agreement accepted by the State.
- Tribal farmers and forest dwellers cultivating forest land under the Forest Rights Act can also be insured.
- Joining is voluntary for all farmers, including those who have a Kisan Credit Card or crop loan.
- Farmers with a KCC or crop loan for a notified crop are enrolled through their bank automatically unless they opt out in writing at least 7 days before the enrolment cut-off date.
- The farmer must give an Aadhaar number and declare the crop sown or to be sown.
- Enrolment must be done before the cut-off date notified by the State, which normally is not later than 15 July for Kharif, 15 December for Rabi and 15 February for summer crops.
Not eligible:
- Losses caused by war, nuclear risks, malicious damage or other preventable risks are not covered.

Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
- A loan taken only against gold, fixed deposits or other collateral, without insurable interest in notified land and crop, does not qualify for cover.
- Farmers who enrol, or whose premium is debited, after the damaging event has happened cannot claim localized calamity loss for that event.
- Crops that the State has not notified for that area and season are not covered.

Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) — Overview
Crop insurance for farmers, including tenant farmers and sharecroppers, who grow notified crops in notified areas. The farmer pays a small premium (at most 2% for Kharif, 1.5% for Rabi and 5% for commercial or horticultural crops) and is paid for crop loss caused by natural calamities, pests and diseases.
Central government scheme. Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.

question: How much monthly stipend do interns get under the PM Internship Scheme?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Prime Minister Internship Scheme (PMIS) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Must be an Indian national.
- Aged 18 to 25 years on the date the application is submitted.
- Must not be in a full-time job.
- Must have passed Class 10 (High School) or Class 12, or hold an ITI certificate or a polytechnic diploma, or a graduate degree (such as BA, B.Sc., B.Com, BCA, BBA, B.Pharma, B.E./B.Tech) or a postgraduate degree (such as MA, M.Sc., M.Com, MCA, M.Tech).
- Must not be in full-time education; however, people in online or distance courses, and final-year full-time graduate or postgraduate students, can apply.
- Final-year students must submit a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from their institution confirming the internship will not affect their studies.
Not eligible:
- Graduates or postgraduates of IITs, IIMs, National Law Universities, IISER, NIDs, IIITs and IISc.
- Holders of CA, CMA, CS, MBBS, BDS, MD, MS, MBA (or equivalent), MPhil or PhD.
- Anyone currently in a skill, apprenticeship, internship or training programme under a Central or State Government scheme, or who has ever completed apprenticeship or training under NATS or NAPS.

Prime Minister Internship Scheme (PMIS) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
- Anyone whose own income, or the income of a parent or spouse, was more than Rs 12 lakh (Rs 12,00,000) in the previous financial year.
- Anyone who, or whose parent or spouse, is a permanent or regular government employee (Central or State Government, UT administration, PSU, statutory body or local body); contractual employees do not count.

Prime Minister Internship Scheme (PMIS) — Overview
Offers paid internships of 6 or 9 months in top companies to Indian youth aged 18 to 25 who are not in full-time jobs. Interns get Rs 9,000 a month, a one-time grant of Rs 6,000 and insurance cover. It is still a pilot project, extended until December 2026, and applications are taken on a rolling basis.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Corporate Affairs.

National Family Benefit Scheme (NFBS) — Eligibility rules
- The household must be below the poverty line (BPL).
- The person who died must have been the household's main earner (breadwinner).
- The breadwinner must have been aged 18 to 59 years at the time of death.
- Any death counts, whether natural, accidental or from any other cause.
- A woman who was a homemaker also counts as a breadwinner.
- The money is paid to the surviving family member who, after a local inquiry, is found to be the new head of the household.
- Household means the spouse, minor children, unmarried daughters and dependent parents; if the person who died was an unmarried adult, it means minor brothers and sisters and dependent parents.
Not eligible:
- Households that are not BPL are not covered by the central scheme.
- Deaths of a breadwinner aged 60 or above, or below 18, are not covered.
- The scheme pays only on the death of the breadwinner, not of other family members.

National Family Benefit Scheme (NFBS) — Eligibility rules
- The household must be below the poverty line (BPL).
- The person who died must have been the household's main earner (breadwinner).
- The breadwinner must have been aged 18 to 59 years at the time of death.
- Any death counts, whether natural, accidental or from any other cause.
- A woman who was a homemaker also counts as a breadwinner.
- The money is paid to the surviving family member who, after a local inquiry, is found to be the new head of the household.
- Household means the spouse, minor children, unmarried daughters and dependent parents; if the person who died was an unmarried adult, it means minor brothers and sisters and dependent parents.
Not eligible:
- Households that are not BPL are not covered by the central scheme.
- Deaths of a breadwinner aged 60 or above, or below 18, are not covered.
- The scheme pays only on the death of the breadwinner, not of other family members.

question: पीएमकेवीवाई में दिव्यांग उम्मीदवार के सहायक उपकरणों के लिए कितनी सहायता मिलती है?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Scheme of Assistance to Persons with Disabilities for Purchase/Fitting of Aids/Appliances (ADIP Scheme) (ADIP) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Must be an Indian citizen; there is no age limit.
- Must have a disability of at least 40%, shown by a UDID card (or UDID enrolment number) together with a disability certificate.
- Must give an Aadhaar number or Aadhaar enrolment ID.
- The person's own monthly income from all sources must be Rs 30,000 or less.
- For a dependant (such as a child), the monthly income of the parents or guardians must be Rs 30,000 or less.
- Must not have received help for the same purpose from any source in the last 3 years; for children below 18, custom items like orthosis, prosthesis and learning material can be given again after 1 year.
- For a motorised tricycle or motorised wheelchair: aged 16 years or above with at least 80% disability (severe locomotor disability, stroke, cerebral palsy, hemiplegia or similar), given once in five years.
Not eligible:
- People whose monthly income (or parents'/guardians' income, for dependants) is more than Rs 30,000.
- People who received an aid for the same purpose from any source in the last 3 years.
- People with disability below 40% (except some school children covered under ADIP-SSA through a joint certificate).

Scheme of Assistance to Persons with Disabilities for Purchase/Fitting of Aids/Appliances (ADIP Scheme) (ADIP) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
- People aged 16 and above with cognitive impairment cannot get a motorised tricycle or motorised wheelchair, for safety reasons.

Scheme of Assistance to Persons with Disabilities for Purchase/Fitting of Aids/Appliances (ADIP Scheme) (ADIP) — Overview
ADIP gives people with disabilities durable aids and assistive devices such as wheelchairs, tricycles, artificial limbs, calipers and hearing aids, free or at half cost, depending on income. It is open to Indian citizens of any age with at least 40% disability and a monthly income of Rs 30,000 or less.
Central government scheme. Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (Divyangjan), Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

question: मेरी पढ़ाई बीच में छूट गई है और मैं बेरोजगार हूँ, क्या सरकार मुफ्त में कोई हुनर सिखाने वाली ट्रेनिंग और सर्टिफिकेट देती है?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) — Eligibility rules
- Must be a young person from a poor family living in a rural area.
- Aged 15 to 35 years.
- The upper age limit is 45 years for women, Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs), persons with disabilities, transgender persons and other special groups such as rescued bonded labourers, trafficking victims, manual scavengers and people living with HIV.
- The household's poverty can be shown by any one of these: a BPL card, a BPL PDS or Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) card, or an RSBY card.
- Family members of a member of a registered Self Help Group (SHG) in the village are eligible.
- Families of MGNREGA workers who did at least 15 days of work in the last 12 months are eligible.
Not eligible:
- Youth younger than 15, or older than 35 (older than 45 for women and special groups), cannot join.
- Youth whose household has none of the listed poverty proofs and has not been identified as poor through the village poverty identification process are not eligible.

Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) — Benefits
- Training is completely free: there are no fees for registration, training, exams, certification or placement.
- Courses last 3 to 12 months (576 to 2,304 hours), including on-the-job training at a workplace.
- Free uniform, books and study material; free food and stay in residential courses.
- A government-recognised certificate after passing the final assessment (at least 70% marks needed).
- Help to get a job with regular monthly wages at or above minimum wages, and help to move to a new city if the job needs it.
- After placement, a monthly post-placement support amount is paid into the candidate's bank account for some months (older rule: Rs 1,000 a month for 2 to 6 months; DDU-GKY 2.0 draft procedures: Rs 1,270 a month for 6 months).

PM-Vidyalaxmi Scheme (Pradhan Mantri Vidyalaxmi) (PM-Vidyalaxmi) — Eligibility rules
- Has secured admission in a Quality Higher Educational Institution (QHEI) identified by the Ministry of Education.
- Admission should be on merit, for example through a recognised entrance exam or the merit quota.
- To get the 3% interest subvention, annual family income must be Rs 8 lakh or less, and the subvention applies to loans up to Rs 10 lakh.
- The 3% interest subvention is limited to 1 lakh students a year, chosen in this order of preference: admission to a government institution, then technical/professional courses, then students who passed Class 12 or Class 10 from a government school, then those who passed Class 12 from a rural school, then girl students.
- Aadhaar is required to get the scheme's benefits, including the loan, interest subvention and credit guarantee.
Not eligible:
- Education loans for admissions under management quota are not eligible.

question: How much subsidy does a general category person get under PM Matsya Sampada Yojana?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Fishers, fish farmers, fish workers and fish vendors can apply as individuals.
- Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, women and differently abled persons are listed beneficiaries; SC, ST and women get the higher rate of assistance.
- Self Help Groups, Joint Liability Groups, fisheries cooperatives, Fish Farmer Producer Organisations, and entrepreneurs or private firms can also apply.
- The project must be a beneficiary-oriented activity listed under the scheme and backed by a Detailed Project Report or self-contained proposal.
- The applicant must already have the land or water body, owned or on lease; a land lease should normally be at least 10 years for infrastructure projects and 7 years for other projects.
- For livelihood support during the fishing ban, the person must be a full-time active traditional fisher, below the poverty line, aged 18 to 60, and a member of a fishers' cooperative or other registered body.
Not eligible:
- No assistance is given for buying, leasing or acquiring land.
- A project that already gets central funding for the same work in the same location is not funded again.

Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
- If the beneficiary ends the lease early or transfers the assets before the lease period ends, all central assistance must be paid back with 12% yearly penal interest.
- Proposals that are not viable or lack land, clearances or permissions are rejected, and their preparation costs are not reimbursed.

Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) — Benefits
- General category beneficiaries get government assistance of up to 40% of the project or unit cost.
- SC, ST and women beneficiaries get government assistance of up to 60% of the project or unit cost.
- The beneficiary pays the rest from own money or a bank loan; for example, on a Rs 1 lakh project the government pays at most Rs 40,000 for general category and Rs 60,000 for SC, ST and women.
- Each activity has a unit cost ceiling; Himalayan, North-Eastern and island areas may get up to 20% higher unit costs.
- Livelihood and nutritional support in the fishing ban or lean period: the fisher saves Rs 1,500 a year, the government adds Rs 3,000, and the total of Rs 4,500 is paid at Rs 1,500 a month.
- Accident insurance for fishers with the full premium paid by government: Rs 5 lakh for death or permanent total disability, Rs 2.5 lakh for permanent partial disability and Rs 25,000 for accidental hospitalisation.

- Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, women and differently abled persons are listed beneficiaries; SC, ST and women get the higher rate of assistance.
- Self Help Groups, Joint Liability Groups, fisheries cooperatives, Fish Farmer Producer Organisations, and entrepreneurs or private firms can also apply.
- The project must be a beneficiary-oriented activity listed under the scheme and backed by a Detailed Project Report or self-contained proposal.
- The applicant must already have the land or water body, owned or on lease; a land lease should normally be at least 10 years for infrastructure projects and 7 years for other projects.
- For livelihood support during the fishing ban, the person must be a full-time active traditional fisher, below the poverty line, aged 18 to 60, and a member of a fishers' cooperative or other registered body.
Not eligible:
- No assistance is given for buying, leasing or acquiring land.
- A project that already gets central funding for the same work in the same location is not funded again.

Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
- If the beneficiary ends the lease early or transfers the assets before the lease period ends, all central assistance must be paid back with 12% yearly penal interest.
- Proposals that are not viable or lack land, clearances or permissions are rejected, and their preparation costs are not reimbursed.

Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) — Benefits
- General category beneficiaries get government assistance of up to 40% of the project or unit cost.
- SC, ST and women beneficiaries get government assistance of up to 60% of the project or unit cost.
- The beneficiary pays the rest from own money or a bank loan; for example, on a Rs 1 lakh project the government pays at most Rs 40,000 for general category and Rs 60,000 for SC, ST and women.
- Each activity has a unit cost ceiling; Himalayan, North-Eastern and island areas may get up to 20% higher unit costs.
- Livelihood and nutritional support in the fishing ban or lean period: the fisher saves Rs 1,500 a year, the government adds Rs 3,000, and the total of Rs 4,500 is paid at Rs 1,500 a month.
- Accident insurance for fishers with the full premium paid by government: Rs 5 lakh for death or permanent total disability, Rs 2.5 lakh for permanent partial disability and Rs 25,000 for accidental hospitalisation.

- Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, women and differently abled persons are listed beneficiaries; SC, ST and women get the higher rate of assistance.
- Self Help Groups, Joint Liability Groups, fisheries cooperatives, Fish Farmer Producer Organisations, and entrepreneurs or private firms can also apply.
- The project must be a beneficiary-oriented activity listed under the scheme and backed by a Detailed Project Report or self-contained proposal.
- The applicant must already have the land or water body, owned or on lease; a land lease should normally be at least 10 years for infrastructure projects and 7 years for other projects.
- For livelihood support during the fishing ban, the person must be a full-time active traditional fisher, below the poverty line, aged 18 to 60, and a member of a fishers' cooperative or other registered body.
Not eligible:
- No assistance is given for buying, leasing or acquiring land.
- A project that already gets central funding for the same work in the same location is not funded again.

Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
- If the beneficiary ends the lease early or transfers the assets before the lease period ends, all central assistance must be paid back with 12% yearly penal interest.
- Proposals that are not viable or lack land, clearances or permissions are rejected, and their preparation costs are not reimbursed.

Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) — Benefits
- General category beneficiaries get government assistance of up to 40% of the project or unit cost.
- SC, ST and women beneficiaries get government assistance of up to 60% of the project or unit cost.
- The beneficiary pays the rest from own money or a bank loan; for example, on a Rs 1 lakh project the government pays at most Rs 40,000 for general category and Rs 60,000 for SC, ST and women.
- Each activity has a unit cost ceiling; Himalayan, North-Eastern and island areas may get up to 20% higher unit costs.
- Livelihood and nutritional support in the fishing ban or lean period: the fisher saves Rs 1,500 a year, the government adds Rs 3,000, and the total of Rs 4,500 is paid at Rs 1,500 a month.
- Accident insurance for fishers with the full premium paid by government: Rs 5 lakh for death or permanent total disability, Rs 2.5 lakh for permanent partial disability and Rs 25,000 for accidental hospitalisation.

question: What is the maximum Shishu loan under PM MUDRA Yojana?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) — Eligibility rules
- Meant for micro enterprises (small businesses) that need institutional credit.
- The loan must be for a non-agricultural activity; allied activities such as poultry, dairy and beekeeping are also covered.
- The loan can be for a term loan, working capital, or both.
- Tarun Plus loans (above Rs 10 lakh) are only for entrepreneurs who took and fully repaid an earlier loan under the Tarun category.
Not eligible:
- Farming itself is not covered; the loan is for non-agricultural purposes and allied activities only.

Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) — Benefits
- Shishu: loan of up to Rs 50,000.
- Kishore: loan above Rs 50,000 and up to Rs 5 lakh.
- Tarun: loan above Rs 5 lakh and up to Rs 10 lakh.
- Tarun Plus: loan above Rs 10 lakh and up to Rs 20 lakh, available from 24 October 2024 to those who repaid an earlier Tarun loan.
- No collateral (security) is required.

Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) — Overview
Loans without collateral for micro enterprises doing non-farm business, or allied activities such as poultry, dairy and beekeeping. Banks, NBFCs and microfinance institutions give the loans in four categories: Shishu (up to Rs 50,000), Kishore (up to Rs 5 lakh), Tarun (up to Rs 10 lakh) and Tarun Plus (up to Rs 20 lakh, for those who repaid a Tarun loan).
Central government scheme. Ministry of Finance, Department of Financial Services.

Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Meant for rural poor households: at least one member of each identified poor household, preferably a woman, is brought into a Self Help Group.
- Poor households are identified by the community through the Participatory Identification of Poor (PIP) process, and the list is vetted by the Gram Sabha; the BPL list alone is not used.
- SHGs usually have 10 to 20 members, mostly women; special SHGs in remote tribal or difficult areas, or of vulnerable people such as persons with disabilities, may have as few as 5 members.
- Groups of persons with disabilities, elderly people or transgender persons may include both men and women; other SHGs are women's groups.
- To get the Revolving Fund, an SHG should have existed for at least 3 to 6 months, follow the Panchasutras and not have received a Revolving Fund before.
- To get a bank loan, an SHG must have been active for at least 6 months as per its books of account and follow the Panchasutras: regular meetings, regular savings, regular inter-loaning, timely repayment and up-to-date books.
- The SHG must qualify under the grading norms fixed by NABARD.

Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) — Eligibility rules
- Any individual above 18 years of age can apply.
- There is no income limit.

Not eligible:

- Projects with no capital expenditure are not financed.
- Activities on the scheme's negative list, or banned by local authorities, are not allowed.
- The cost of land cannot be counted in the project cost.

question: I belong to a Scheduled Caste, just passed Class 10, and my father earns about 2 lakh a year. Which scholarship will pay my fees and give me some money every year for Class 11, 12 and college?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Post Matric Scholarship to the Students belonging to Scheduled Castes for Studies in India (PMS-SC) — Eligibility rules
- You must be an Indian national.
- You must belong to a Scheduled Caste notified for the State/UT where you are domiciled.
- You must have passed Class 10 (matriculation) or a higher exam from a recognised board or university.
- Parents' or guardian's income from all sources must not exceed Rs 2,50,000 in the last financial year.
- You must study a recognised post-matric course (Class 11-12, ITI, diploma, graduation, postgraduation, PhD etc.) at a recognised institution in India.
- All children of the same parents can get the scholarship; there is no limit on the number of children.
- To keep getting it each year, you need satisfactory academic performance and at least 75% attendance.
Not eligible:
- Students admitted on management quota, NRI quota, spot admission or other seats not filled on merit.
- Students who finish one stage and then study the same stage again in another subject, e.g. B.Com after B.A.
- Students who accept another scholarship or stipend at the same time; they must choose one.
- Studies abroad are not covered.
- Students who got the scholarship through false statements are blacklisted from all scholarships.

Post Matric Scholarship to the Students belonging to Scheduled Castes for Studies in India (PMS-SC) — Overview
A centrally sponsored scholarship for Scheduled Caste students studying after Class 10 (from Class 11 up to PhD) whose parents earn up to Rs 2.5 lakh a year. It pays the compulsory non-refundable fees, including tuition, plus a yearly academic allowance of Rs 2,500 to Rs 13,500. The student's home State/UT runs it.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Department of Social Justice and Empowerment.

Post Matric Scholarship for Students Belonging to Scheduled Tribes for Studies in India (PMS-ST) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Belongs to a Scheduled Tribe notified for the student's own (domicile) state or union territory.
- Has passed Class 10 (matriculation) or a higher exam and is studying a recognised post-matric course, from Class 11 up to post-graduation, in India.
- Family income from all sources must be Rs 2,50,000 a year or less (income of the father and mother is counted; earnings of siblings or other relatives are not).
- An orphan supported by a guardian does not have to meet the income limit.
- Has a bank account in the student's own name, linked to Aadhaar and a mobile number.
- Does not hold any other scholarship at the same time; if offered another one, the student must choose one of them.
- The course must be at a recognised institution, such as a government college or university, a recognised private university or professional college, a Class 11-12 school, a polytechnic or an ITI.
Not eligible:
- Students admitted to one of the Ministry's listed top class institutes (252 at the time of the guidelines) are covered by the National Fellowship and Scholarship for Higher Education of ST Students instead of this scheme.

question: मैं अनुसूचित जनजाति से हूँ, 11वीं कक्षा में दाखिला लिया है और घर की आमदनी बहुत कम है। क्या सरकार से फीस और हर महीने वजीफा मिल सकता है?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin (PMAY-G) — Eligibility rules
- You must live in a rural area (a village).
- Your household has no house, or lives in a kutcha house.
- Your present house has no more than 2 rooms.
- No member of your household owns a pucca house.
- Families are chosen from the SECC 2011 housing-deprivation data and the Awaas+ survey lists, and the Gram Sabha checks the list.
- These families get top priority (automatic inclusion): those with no shelter, destitute families living on alms, manual scavengers, Primitive Tribal Group families and legally freed bonded labourers.
Not eligible:
- Anyone in the household owns a motorised three-wheeler or four-wheeler, or mechanised three- or four-wheeler farm equipment.
- Anyone in the household has a Kisan Credit Card with a limit of Rs 50,000 or more.
- Any household member is a government employee, or the household runs a non-farm business registered with the government.
- Any household member earns more than Rs 15,000 a month.
- Anyone in the household pays income tax or professional tax.
- The household owns 2.5 acres or more of irrigated land, or 5 acres or more of unirrigated land.

Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin (PMAY-G) — Benefits
- Rs 1.20 lakh to build a pucca house in plain areas.
- Rs 1.30 lakh in hill states and UTs (Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh), North-Eastern states, difficult areas and IAP districts.
- Up to 90/95 days of unskilled wage work under MGNREGS for building your own house, on top of the grant.
- Rs 12,000 for a toilet, through Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen), MGNREGS or another funding source.
- The house must be at least 25 square metres, with a space for clean cooking. Officials also help with house designs and trained masons.
- If you want one, officials help you get a bank loan of up to Rs 70,000. All payments go by DBT into your Aadhaar-linked bank or post office account.

Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban 2.0 (PMAY-U 2.0) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Your family lives in an urban area (a statutory town or a notified planning or development area).
- No member of your family owns a pucca house anywhere in India.
- Your annual household income is up to Rs 9 lakh (Rs 9,00,000). EWS means up to Rs 3 lakh, LIG means Rs 3 lakh to Rs 6 lakh, and MIG means Rs 6 lakh to Rs 9 lakh.
- 'Family' means husband, wife and unmarried sons and/or unmarried daughters.
- Only EWS families (income up to Rs 3 lakh) can get help to build a house on their own land (BLC) or to own a house in a partnership project (AHP). For BLC you need your own land or a land patta from the state.
- The home-loan interest subsidy (ISS) is for EWS, LIG and MIG families. The loan must be up to Rs 25 lakh, the house worth up to Rs 35 lakh and the carpet area up to 120 sq m, and the loan must be sanctioned and paid out on or after 1 September 2024.
- Every family member must have Aadhaar or an Aadhaar Virtual ID.
Not eligible:
- You cannot apply if you were given a house under any Central, State or local government housing scheme in the last 20 years, in a town or a village.
- You cannot apply if your family owns a pucca house anywhere in India.

question: We are a poor family in a village and still cook on wood because we have no gas connection. Is there a government scheme that gives a free LPG connection to women?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) — Eligibility rules
- The applicant must be a woman who is at least 18 years old.
- No one in the household should already have an LPG connection from any oil marketing company.
- The household must fall in one of the listed groups: SC or ST households, PMAY-Gramin beneficiaries, Most Backward Classes, Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) card holders, tea and ex-tea garden tribes, forest dwellers, people living on islands or river islands, or SECC (AHL TIN) households.
- A poor household outside these groups can still qualify by giving a 14-point deprivation declaration in the set format.
- Migrant families can apply by giving a self-declaration in place of address proof and a ration card.
Not eligible:
- Households where any family member already has an LPG connection.
- Women under 18 years of age.
- Men cannot get the connection in their own name; it is issued to an adult woman of the household.

Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) — Overview
Gives adult women from poor households that have no LPG connection a deposit-free cooking gas connection. The government pays Rs 2,050 towards a 14.2 kg cylinder connection, and the first refill and the stove are also free.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.

Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) — Benefits
- A deposit-free LPG connection: the Government of India pays Rs 2,050 for a 14.2 kg cylinder connection or Rs 1,300 for a 5 kg cylinder connection.
- This amount covers the cylinder security deposit (Rs 1,700 for 14.2 kg or Rs 950 for 5 kg), the pressure regulator (Rs 150), the LPG hose (Rs 100), the consumer card (Rs 25) and inspection or installation charges (Rs 75).
- The first LPG refill and the stove (hotplate) are given free by the oil company along with the connection.
- The family can choose a 14.2 kg single cylinder, a 5 kg single cylinder or a 5 kg double cylinder connection.

question: मेरे घर में अभी तक गैस कनेक्शन नहीं है और हम गरीब परिवार हैं, मुझे मुफ्त गैस कनेक्शन कैसे मिलेगा?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (PMSG: MBY) — Eligibility rules
- Must be a residential electricity consumer with a valid consumer account number from the local electricity distribution company (DISCOM).
- The solar plant must be grid-connected and linked to that household's residential power connection.
- Panels must be on a roof, terrace or balcony, or on an elevated structure (ground-mounted elevated structures are allowed).
- The system must be installed by a vendor registered on the PM Surya Ghar National Portal.
- Solar modules must be made in India from Indian-made cells (Domestic Content Requirement).
- Group housing societies and RWAs can get the subsidy for common facilities, including EV charging, up to 500 kW, counted at 3 kW per house.
Not eligible:
- Non-residential connections such as government, commercial and industrial users get no subsidy.
- Off-grid systems that are not connected to the grid are not eligible.
- Systems using imported (non-DCR) solar modules are not eligible.
- A system that is shifted to a new location cannot get the subsidy again; it is given only once per installation.
- A home that already got a central rooftop solar subsidy can claim only for added capacity, up to 3 kW in total.

PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (PMSG: MBY) — Overview
Gives households a central subsidy of up to Rs 78,000 to put grid-connected solar panels on their roof. The aim is up to 300 units of free or low-cost electricity a month. The scheme is set to run until 31 March 2027.
Central government scheme. Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.

question: What is the minimum age to get devices under Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY) — Eligibility rules
- Must be a senior citizen aged 60 years or above.
- Must belong to the BPL category, shown by a BPL ration card, proof of old age pension under IGNOAPS or a state/UT pension scheme, or a certificate from the district authority.
- Seniors who are not BPL can also apply if their monthly income from all sources is Rs 15,000 or less.
- Must have an age-related disability or infirmity, such as low vision, hearing loss, loss of teeth or difficulty in walking.
- Must have an Aadhaar card or Aadhaar enrolment slip.
- A medical officer's certificate is needed for loss of vision, hearing impairment, loss of teeth, or locomotor disability needing a wheelchair.
Not eligible:
- People below 60 years of age.
- Non-BPL seniors whose monthly income from all sources is more than Rs 15,000.
- Anyone who received the same device free from any government source (including local bodies and public undertakings) in the last 3 years.

Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY) — Overview
RVY gives free assisted-living devices such as walking sticks, walkers, wheelchairs, hearing aids, spectacles and dentures to senior citizens aged 60 or above who have an age-related disability or infirmity. Seniors must be from a BPL family or have a monthly income of Rs 15,000 or less.
Central government scheme. Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (implemented by ALIMCO).

Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY) — How to apply
- Attend an RVY camp in your district, where seniors are assessed and devices are then distributed.
- Or visit an ALIMCO production centre or regional marketing centre (OPD mode) to be assessed and get the device.
- Call ALIMCO's toll-free number 1800-180-5129 to find the nearest centre or camp.

question: Mere dadaji 68 saal ke hain, unke daant gir gaye hain aur chashma bhi chahiye, ghar ki kamai 10,000 mahina hai. Sarkar se muft upkaran kaise milega?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin (PMAY-G) — Eligibility rules
- You must live in a rural area (a village).
- Your household has no house, or lives in a kutcha house.
- Your present house has no more than 2 rooms.
- No member of your household owns a pucca house.
- Families are chosen from the SECC 2011 housing-deprivation data and the Awaas+ survey lists, and the Gram Sabha checks the list.
- These families get top priority (automatic inclusion): those with no shelter, destitute families living on alms, manual scavengers, Primitive Tribal Group families and legally freed bonded labourers.
Not eligible:
- Anyone in the household owns a motorised three-wheeler or four-wheeler, or mechanised three- or four-wheeler farm equipment.
- Anyone in the household has a Kisan Credit Card with a limit of Rs 50,000 or more.
- Any household member is a government employee, or the household runs a non-farm business registered with the government.
- Any household member earns more than Rs 15,000 a month.
- Anyone in the household pays income tax or professional tax.
- The household owns 2.5 acres or more of irrigated land, or 5 acres or more of unirrigated land.

Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin (PMAY-G) — Benefits
- Rs 1.20 lakh to build a pucca house in plain areas.
- Rs 1.30 lakh in hill states and UTs (Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh), North-Eastern states, difficult areas and IAP districts.
- Up to 90/95 days of unskilled wage work under MGNREGS for building your own house, on top of the grant.
- Rs 12,000 for a toilet, through Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen), MGNREGS or another funding source.
- The house must be at least 25 square metres, with a space for clean cooking. Officials also help with house designs and trained masons.
- If you want one, officials help you get a bank loan of up to Rs 70,000. All payments go by DBT into your Aadhaar-linked bank or post office account.

Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin (PMAY-G) — Overview
PMAY-G gives money to poor rural families who have no house or live in a kutcha house so they can build a pucca house. The grant is Rs 1.20 lakh in plain areas and Rs 1.30 lakh in hill, north-eastern and difficult areas. The scheme is still running: its second phase adds 2 crore more houses, and the overall target is 4.95 crore houses by March 2029.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Rural Development (Department of Rural Development).

question: For how many days a year does the Anganwadi give food under Poshan 2.0?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 – Supplementary Nutrition (Poshan 2.0) — Eligibility rules
- Children aged 6 months to 6 years get supplementary nutrition.
- Pregnant women, and mothers for up to 6 months after the birth.
- Adolescent girls aged 14 to 18 years, but only in Aspirational Districts and in Assam and the other North-Eastern states.
- Anyone who qualifies can join. There is no caste, religion or income condition.
- The beneficiary must register at the nearest Anganwadi Centre with Aadhaar. A child can be registered using the mother's Aadhaar.
- Families staying in an Anganwadi area, even for a short time, can register there. A registration can be moved to the new centre through Poshan Tracker.
Not eligible:
- Food is given only to people registered at an Anganwadi Centre.
- Adolescent girls outside Aspirational Districts and the North-Eastern states (including Assam) are not covered.

Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 – Supplementary Nutrition (Poshan 2.0) — Benefits
- Food is given for at least 300 days a year, about 25 days a month.
- Children aged 3 to 6 years get a morning snack and a hot cooked meal at the Anganwadi.
- Children aged 6 months to 3 years, pregnant women, breastfeeding mothers, severely malnourished children and eligible adolescent girls get take-home ration (prepared food, not raw grain). It is given twice a month, preferably on the 1st and 15th.
- Daily food norm: 500 kcal and 12 to 15 g protein for children aged 6 to 72 months, and 800 kcal and 20 to 25 g protein for severely malnourished children.
- Daily food norm: 600 kcal and 18 to 20 g protein for pregnant women, breastfeeding mothers and adolescent girls.
- The Anganwadi also gives pre-school education, nutrition and health education, vaccination, health check-ups and referrals to hospitals.

Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 – Supplementary Nutrition (Poshan 2.0) — Overview
Anganwadi Centres give extra food (supplementary nutrition) to children aged 6 months to 6 years, to pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers, and to adolescent girls aged 14 to 18 in Aspirational Districts and North-Eastern states. There is no caste, religion or income condition; the person only has to register at the nearest Anganwadi Centre.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Women and Child Development.

National Food Security Act, 2013 - Priority Households, with Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) (NFSA / PMGKAY) — Eligibility rules
- The household must be identified by its State/UT government as a Priority Household (PHH) and hold an NFSA ration card.
- Each state sets its own criteria for priority households, so the rules differ from state to state.
- Nationally, up to 75% of the rural population and up to 50% of the urban population can be covered; each state has its own coverage percentage.
- The eldest woman of the household aged 18 years or more is named head of the household on the ration card; if there is no such woman, the eldest man is head until a female member turns 18.
- The Centre has told states to include eligible persons with disabilities, persons affected by leprosy and children born after 2011.
Not eligible:
- Households not identified by the state as priority households or Antyodaya households are not covered.
- Total coverage in each state is fixed using Census 2011 figures; the ceiling can be raised only after data from the next census is published.
- Ineligible, fake or duplicate ration cards, and members who have died or migrated, are removed when states verify their lists.

These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 – Supplementary Nutrition (Poshan 2.0) — Eligibility rules
- Children aged 6 months to 6 years get supplementary nutrition.
- Pregnant women, and mothers for up to 6 months after the birth.
- Adolescent girls aged 14 to 18 years, but only in Aspirational Districts and in Assam and the other North-Eastern states.
- Anyone who qualifies can join. There is no caste, religion or income condition.
- The beneficiary must register at the nearest Anganwadi Centre with Aadhaar. A child can be registered using the mother's Aadhaar.
- Families staying in an Anganwadi area, even for a short time, can register there. A registration can be moved to the new centre through Poshan Tracker.
Not eligible:
- Food is given only to people registered at an Anganwadi Centre.
- Adolescent girls outside Aspirational Districts and the North-Eastern states (including Assam) are not covered.

Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 – Supplementary Nutrition (Poshan 2.0) — Overview
Anganwadi Centres give extra food (supplementary nutrition) to children aged 6 months to 6 years, to pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers, and to adolescent girls aged 14 to 18 in Aspirational Districts and North-Eastern states. There is no caste, religion or income condition; the person only has to register at the nearest Anganwadi Centre.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Women and Child Development.

Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 – Supplementary Nutrition (Poshan 2.0) — Benefits
- Food is given for at least 300 days a year, about 25 days a month.
- Children aged 3 to 6 years get a morning snack and a hot cooked meal at the Anganwadi.
- Children aged 6 months to 3 years, pregnant women, breastfeeding mothers, severely malnourished children and eligible adolescent girls get take-home ration (prepared food, not raw grain). It is given twice a month, preferably on the 1st and 15th.
- Daily food norm: 500 kcal and 12 to 15 g protein for children aged 6 to 72 months, and 800 kcal and 20 to 25 g protein for severely malnourished children.
- Daily food norm: 600 kcal and 18 to 20 g protein for pregnant women, breastfeeding mothers and adolescent girls.
- The Anganwadi also gives pre-school education, nutrition and health education, vaccination, health check-ups and referrals to hospitals.

question: Poshan 2.0 me take home ration mahine me kitni baar milta hai?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban 2.0 (PMAY-U 2.0) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Your family lives in an urban area (a statutory town or a notified planning or development area).
- No member of your family owns a pucca house anywhere in India.
- Your annual household income is up to Rs 9 lakh (Rs 9,00,000). EWS means up to Rs 3 lakh, LIG means Rs 3 lakh to Rs 6 lakh, and MIG means Rs 6 lakh to Rs 9 lakh.
- 'Family' means husband, wife and unmarried sons and/or unmarried daughters.
- Only EWS families (income up to Rs 3 lakh) can get help to build a house on their own land (BLC) or to own a house in a partnership project (AHP). For BLC you need your own land or a land patta from the state.
- The home-loan interest subsidy (ISS) is for EWS, LIG and MIG families. The loan must be up to Rs 25 lakh, the house worth up to Rs 35 lakh and the carpet area up to 120 sq m, and the loan must be sanctioned and paid out on or after 1 September 2024.
- Every family member must have Aadhaar or an Aadhaar Virtual ID.
Not eligible:
- You cannot apply if you were given a house under any Central, State or local government housing scheme in the last 20 years, in a town or a village.
- You cannot apply if your family owns a pucca house anywhere in India.

Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban 2.0 (PMAY-U 2.0) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
- Families whose PMAY-U houses were cancelled (curtailed) after 31 December 2023 cannot get them sanctioned again under PMAY-U 2.0.
- No interest subsidy if the loan is above Rs 25 lakh or the house is worth more than Rs 35 lakh.
- No interest subsidy if an earlier owner already took the subsidy on the same property, or if you claim it again after moving your loan to another lender.

Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban 2.0 (PMAY-U 2.0) — Overview
PMAY-U 2.0 helps urban families who own no pucca house anywhere in India and earn up to Rs 9 lakh a year to build, buy or rent a home. Poorer (EWS) families can get about Rs 2.5 lakh of government help per house, and home-loan borrowers can get an interest subsidy of up to Rs 1.80 lakh. It runs for 5 years from 1 September 2024.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.

- Ineligible, fake or duplicate ration cards, and members who have died or migrated, are removed when states verify their lists.

question: We are a poor family in a village and we don't have a toilet at home. Can we get money from the government to build one?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) - Individual Household Latrine (IHHL) incentive (SBM-G IHHL) — Eligibility rules
- All Below Poverty Line (BPL) households in rural areas.
- Above Poverty Line (APL) households that belong to a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe.
- APL households of small and marginal farmers.
- APL landless labourers who have a homestead.
- APL households with a physically handicapped member.
- APL households headed by a woman.
- The incentive is only for new eligible households, such as new families that do not yet have a toilet.
Not eligible:
- APL households that are not in the listed groups get no incentive. They are encouraged to build a toilet with their own money.
- Households already covered earlier do not get the incentive again.

Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) - Individual Household Latrine (IHHL) incentive (SBM-G IHHL) — Overview
Under Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen), eligible rural households that do not have a toilet get Rs 12,000 to build and use one. It covers all BPL families and certain poorer APL families. The mission is now in Phase II, which mainly aims to keep villages open-defecation free, and only new eligible households get the incentive.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Jal Shakti (Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation).

Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) - Individual Household Latrine (IHHL) incentive (SBM-G IHHL) — Benefits
- An incentive of Rs 12,000 to build a household toilet. This also covers water storage for handwashing and keeping the toilet clean.
- The Centre pays Rs 7,200 (60%) and the State Rs 4,800 (40%). In North-Eastern and special-category states, the Centre pays Rs 10,800 (90%) and the State Rs 1,200 (10%).
- The money is an incentive, not a full refund. It is meant to be enough for a basic twin-pit toilet, and the family pays any extra cost.
- Families with no space for their own toilet can use Community Managed Sanitation Complexes built in the village.

question: What is the maximum amount I can deposit in the Senior Citizens Savings Scheme?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme (SCSS) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Aged 60 years or above on the day the account is opened.
- Aged 55 or more but below 60 and retired (on superannuation or otherwise): you can open the account only within 3 months of receiving your retirement benefits, and you cannot deposit more than the retirement benefits you received.
- Retired defence services personnel (not civilian defence employees) can open an account from age 50, if they meet the other conditions.
- The account can be in your name alone or joint with your spouse only. In a joint account only the first holder's age counts, and the whole deposit belongs to the first holder.
- You may hold more than one SCSS account, but the total deposit across all of them must not exceed Rs 30 lakh. A husband and wife who are each eligible can each deposit up to Rs 30 lakh.
Not eligible:
- NRIs are not allowed to invest in national small savings schemes such as SCSS.
- People below 55 cannot open an account, except retired defence personnel aged 50 or more, and the spouse of a government employee who died in service after reaching 50.
- People aged 55 to 59 who have not retired cannot open an account.

Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme (SCSS) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
- The legal heir of an employee who died while still in service cannot deposit that employee's terminal benefits in SCSS.

Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme (SCSS) — Overview
A government-backed 5-year savings deposit that pays interest every quarter. It is for people aged 60 or above, some retirees from age 55, and retired defence personnel from age 50. You can deposit from Rs 1,000 up to Rs 30 lakh at a post office or an authorised bank branch.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Finance, Department of Economic Affairs (National Savings Institute); run through post offices and authorised banks.

Sukanya Samriddhi Account Scheme (SSY) — Eligibility rules
- The account is opened in the name of a girl child by her parent or guardian.
- The girl must be aged 9 or younger on the day the account is opened; it cannot be opened once she turns 10.
- Each girl can have only one account.
- A family can open accounts for at most 2 girls; more are allowed only when twins or triplets are born in the first or second birth, backed by an affidavit and birth certificates.
Not eligible:
- A girl who has already turned 10 cannot get a new account.
- A girl who already has an account cannot open a second one.
- A third girl in the same family cannot get an account unless the extra girls are twins or triplets from the first or second birth.

Sukanya Samriddhi Account Scheme (SSY) — How to apply
- Open the account at any post office or authorised bank branch by filling Form-1.
- The parent or guardian runs the account until the girl turns 18; after that she can operate it herself.
- If the minimum Rs 250 is missed in a year, the account can be revived within 15 years of opening by paying Rs 50 penalty for each missed year plus the missed minimum deposits.
- The account can be transferred to any post office or bank anywhere in India.

- The legal heir of an employee who died while still in service cannot deposit that employee's terminal benefits in SCSS.

Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme (SCSS) — Benefits
- Make one lump-sum deposit of at least Rs 1,000, in multiples of Rs 1,000, up to Rs 30 lakh.
- Interest is paid every quarter, on the first working day of April, July, October and January. It can be credited straight to your savings account.
- The deposit matures after 5 years. You can extend it for another 3 years by applying within 1 year of maturity.
- The deposit qualifies for an income tax deduction under Section 80C.
- You can close the account early. Before 1 year, any interest already paid is taken back. Between 1 and 2 years, 1.5% of the deposit is deducted. After 2 years, 1% is deducted. An extended account can be closed without deduction after 1 year of extension.
- If the account holder dies, the deposit with interest goes to the nominee or legal heirs. A spouse who is the joint holder or sole nominee, and who is eligible, can continue the account.

question: मैं 58 साल का हूँ, पिछले हफ्ते रिटायर हुआ हूँ और मुझे PF व ग्रेच्युटी का पैसा मिला है। इसे किस सरकारी योजना में जमा करूँ जिससे हर तिमाही ब्याज मिले?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PM-VBRY) — Eligibility rules
- Joined an establishment covered by EPF between 1 August 2025 and 31 July 2027 (both dates included).
- Is a first-time EPF member, meaning they never contributed to EPF with EPFO or an exempted PF trust before 1 August 2025.
- Has a gross monthly salary of up to Rs 1,00,000 at the time of joining, counting all emoluments.
- Has worked at least 6 completed months in the same establishment (needed for the first instalment).
- Has worked 12 completed months in the same establishment and finished the free online financial literacy course (needed for the second instalment).
- Has a UAN and a bank account seeded with Aadhaar.
Not eligible:
- Anyone who contributed to EPF, with EPFO or an exempted trust, before 1 August 2025 is not a first-timer and cannot get the incentive.
- Employees whose gross monthly salary is above Rs 1,00,000 at joining are not covered.
- Anyone who leaves the job before 6 completed months gets no first instalment.
- Anyone who leaves between 6 and 12 months does not get the second instalment.

Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PM-VBRY) — How to apply
- Employees do not need to apply or register. The incentive is worked out from the monthly PF return (ECR) that the employer files.
- Get a UAN through the employer, or generate it yourself using face authentication on the UMANG app.
- Make sure your bank account is seeded with Aadhaar. Payment is held back until it is.
- Before completing 12 months, finish the free financial literacy course on the EPFO website. Helpline: 14480 or 1800-180-1850 (toll-free).

Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS) — Eligibility rules
- Aged 18 years or above.
- Has a severe disability of 80% or more, or multiple disabilities (two or more disabilities together).
- Persons with dwarfism are also eligible.
- Must belong to a household below the poverty line (BPL).
- If the name is missing from the BPL list but the person is otherwise deserving, officials are told not to leave them out and to check and establish eligibility.
Not eligible:
- People from households that are not BPL are not covered by the central scheme.
- A certified disability below 80% does not meet the central scheme's severity level, unless the person has multiple disabilities; some states run their own disability pensions with different rules.
- The pension can be stopped after the yearly verification if the household is no longer BPL or the person has moved away; it can be restored on appeal if they become eligible again.

question: Up to what age of my daughter can I open a Sukanya Samriddhi account?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Sukanya Samriddhi Account Scheme (SSY) — Eligibility rules
- The account is opened in the name of a girl child by her parent or guardian.
- The girl must be aged 9 or younger on the day the account is opened; it cannot be opened once she turns 10.
- Each girl can have only one account.
- A family can open accounts for at most 2 girls; more are allowed only when twins or triplets are born in the first or second birth, backed by an affidavit and birth certificates.
Not eligible:
- A girl who has already turned 10 cannot get a new account.
- A girl who already has an account cannot open a second one.
- A third girl in the same family cannot get an account unless the extra girls are twins or triplets from the first or second birth.

Sukanya Samriddhi Account Scheme (SSY) — Overview
A government small-savings account for a girl child, opened by her parent or guardian before she turns 10, at a post office or authorised bank. Yearly deposits from Rs 250 to Rs 1.5 lakh earn a government-set interest rate with tax benefits, and the account matures 21 years after opening.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Finance, Department of Economic Affairs (National Savings Institute).

Sukanya Samriddhi Account Scheme (SSY) — How to apply
- Open the account at any post office or authorised bank branch by filling Form-1.
- The parent or guardian runs the account until the girl turns 18; after that she can operate it herself.
- If the minimum Rs 250 is missed in a year, the account can be revived within 15 years of opening by paying Rs 50 penalty for each missed year plus the missed minimum deposits.
- The account can be transferred to any post office or bank anywhere in India.

Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme (SCSS) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Aged 60 years or above on the day the account is opened.

- NRIs are not allowed to invest in national small savings schemes such as SCSS.
- People below 55 cannot open an account, except retired defence personnel aged 50 or more, and the spouse of a government employee who died in service after reaching 50.
- People aged 55 to 59 who have not retired cannot open an account.

question: How many days of work are guaranteed in a year under VB-G RAM G?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) — Eligibility rules
- The household lives in a rural area. The guarantee applies in all rural areas of India from 1 July 2026.
- Work is given to adult members, meaning people who have completed 18 years of age.
- Adult members must be willing to do unskilled manual work.
- The household needs a Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Card. Existing MGNREGA job cards with completed e-KYC stay valid until the new cards are issued.
Not eligible:
- Households in urban areas are not covered; the Act applies only to rural areas.
- Persons below 18 years of age cannot be given work under the scheme.

Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) — Overview
Every rural household whose adult members ask for unskilled manual work has a legal guarantee of at least 125 days of paid work in each financial year. The guarantee came into force on 1 July 2026 and replaced MGNREGA, which was repealed the same day.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Rural Development.

Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) — Benefits (part 1 of 2)
- At least 125 days of wage employment per household in every financial year, up from 100 days under MGNREGA.
- Work must be given within 15 days of applying. If it is not, the State must pay an unemployment allowance: at least one-fourth of the notified wage rate for the first 30 days in the year, and at least one-half for the rest of the year.
- Wages are paid weekly, and in any case within 15 days of the muster roll closing. They go straight into the worker's bank or post office account by DBT. If wages are late, the worker gets delay compensation of 0.05% of the unpaid wages for each day of delay.
- Work is given within 5 km of the applicant's village where possible. If it is farther away (but within the Block), an extra 10% of the wage rate is paid for travel and living costs.
- Worksites must have drinking water, shade and a first-aid kit. Injured workers get free treatment, and if hospitalised, a daily allowance of half the wage rate. If five or more children under five are present, a woman worker is paid to look after them.

question: What are the eligibility rules for the Orunodoi scheme of Assam?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 – Supplementary Nutrition (Poshan 2.0) — Eligibility rules
- Children aged 6 months to 6 years get supplementary nutrition.
- Pregnant women, and mothers for up to 6 months after the birth.
- Adolescent girls aged 14 to 18 years, but only in Aspirational Districts and in Assam and the other North-Eastern states.
- Anyone who qualifies can join. There is no caste, religion or income condition.
- The beneficiary must register at the nearest Anganwadi Centre with Aadhaar. A child can be registered using the mother's Aadhaar.
- Families staying in an Anganwadi area, even for a short time, can register there. A registration can be moved to the new centre through Poshan Tracker.
Not eligible:
- Food is given only to people registered at an Anganwadi Centre.
- Adolescent girls outside Aspirational Districts and the North-Eastern states (including Assam) are not covered.

Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) — Eligibility rules
- Eligibility depends on your family being in the scheme's list of eligible families; most families cannot join just by filling a form.
- In rural areas, SECC 2011 families that meet deprivation criteria D1 to D7 (except D6) are covered, for example SC/ST households and families with no adult male member aged 16 to 59.
- In urban areas, SECC 2011 families of workers in 11 listed occupation groups are covered.
- Households automatically included in SECC 2011, such as destitute families living on alms, are covered.
- Families holding an active RSBY card are also covered.
- In January 2022 the list was widened from 10.74 crore to 12 crore families, and many states cover extra families at their own cost.
- Every person aged 70 or above is covered regardless of income, through the Ayushman Vay Vandana card.
- There is no limit on family size, age or gender.
Not eligible:
- Families not in the eligible list cannot get the card simply by applying; only people aged 70 or above can enrol themselves.
- Seniors aged 70 or above who already get free treatment under CGHS, ECHS, CAPF or a state government health scheme must choose only one scheme.

Scheme of Assistance to Persons with Disabilities for Purchase/Fitting of Aids/Appliances (ADIP Scheme) (ADIP) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Must be an Indian citizen; there is no age limit.
- Must have a disability of at least 40%, shown by a UDID card (or UDID enrolment number) together with a disability certificate.
- Must give an Aadhaar number or Aadhaar enrolment ID.
- The person's own monthly income from all sources must be Rs 30,000 or less.
- For a dependant (such as a child), the monthly income of the parents or guardians must be Rs 30,000 or less.
- Must not have received help for the same purpose from any source in the last 3 years; for children below 18, custom items like orthosis, prosthesis and learning material can be given again after 1 year.
- For a motorised tricycle or motorised wheelchair: aged 16 years or above with at least 80% disability (severe locomotor disability, stroke, cerebral palsy, hemiplegia or similar), given once in five years.
Not eligible:
- People whose monthly income (or parents'/guardians' income, for dependants) is more than Rs 30,000.
- People who received an aid for the same purpose from any source in the last 3 years.
- People with disability below 40% (except some school children covered under ADIP-SSA through a joint certificate).

Central government scheme. Ministry of Education (Department of Higher Education), with the Department of Financial Services.

question: What are the eligibility rules for the Mukhyamantri Chiranjeevi Swasthya Bima Yojana of Rajasthan?

Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- You must be a pregnant woman who gives birth in a health facility: a sub-centre, PHC, CHC, FRU, the general ward of a district or state hospital, or an accredited private institution.
- In the 10 Low Performing States (Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Bihar, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Assam, Rajasthan, Odisha, Jammu and Kashmir), every pregnant woman who delivers in a government health centre qualifies.

Not eligible:
- In the High Performing States, women who are not BPL, SC or ST do not get the cash payment.

Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
- The government does not pay the bill of a private hospital; a woman who chooses an accredited private hospital gets only her fixed cash amount.

Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) — Eligibility rules
- Aged 18 to 50 years when joining.
- Holds an individual or joint savings account with a participating bank or post office.
- Agrees to join and allows the yearly premium to be auto-debited from that account.
- A person can join through only one bank or post office account.
- A member who joined before turning 50 can keep renewing the cover every year up to age 55.
Not eligible:
- New entry is not allowed after the age of 50 years.
- Cover ends on reaching age 55 (age nearest birthday).
- Cover ends if the bank account is closed or does not have enough balance to pay the premium.
- Death from causes other than an accident within the first 30 days of joining is not covered.
- If premium is paid through more than one account, the extra premium is forfeited and total cover stays at Rs 2 lakh.

PM Young Achievers Scholarship Award Scheme for Vibrant India for OBCs and Others (PM YASASVI) (PM YASASVI) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Belongs to the OBC, EBC (economically backward class) or DNT (denotified, nomadic or semi-nomadic tribe) category, with a valid certificate.

Not eligible:

- Family members of a member of a registered Self Help Group (SHG) in the village are eligible.
- Families of MGNREGA workers who did at least 15 days of work in the last 12 months are eligible.
Not eligible:
- Youth younger than 15, or older than 35 (older than 45 for women and special groups), cannot join.
- Youth whose household has none of the listed poverty proofs and has not been identified as poor through the village poverty identification process are not eligible.

Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS) — Eligibility rules
- Aged 18 years or above.
- Has a severe disability of 80% or more, or multiple disabilities (two or more disabilities together).
- Persons with dwarfism are also eligible.
- Must belong to a household below the poverty line (BPL).
- If the name is missing from the BPL list but the person is otherwise deserving, officials are told not to leave them out and to check and establish eligibility.
Not eligible:
- People from households that are not BPL are not covered by the central scheme.
- A certified disability below 80% does not meet the central scheme's severity level, unless the person has multiple disabilities; some states run their own disability pensions with different rules.

- Projects with no capital expenditure are not financed.
- Activities on the scheme's negative list, or banned by local authorities, are not allowed.
- The cost of land cannot be counted in the project cost.

question: What are the eligibility rules for the PM-KUSUM solar pump scheme?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (PMSG: MBY) — Eligibility rules
- Must be a residential electricity consumer with a valid consumer account number from the local electricity distribution company (DISCOM).
- The solar plant must be grid-connected and linked to that household's residential power connection.
- Panels must be on a roof, terrace or balcony, or on an elevated structure (ground-mounted elevated structures are allowed).
- The system must be installed by a vendor registered on the PM Surya Ghar National Portal.
- Solar modules must be made in India from Indian-made cells (Domestic Content Requirement).
- Group housing societies and RWAs can get the subsidy for common facilities, including EV charging, up to 500 kW, counted at 3 kW per house.
Not eligible:
- Non-residential connections such as government, commercial and industrial users get no subsidy.
- Off-grid systems that are not connected to the grid are not eligible.
- Systems using imported (non-DCR) solar modules are not eligible.
- A system that is shifted to a new location cannot get the subsidy again; it is given only once per installation.
- A home that already got a central rooftop solar subsidy can claim only for added capacity, up to 3 kW in total.

Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Your family must own cultivable land, and the names must be entered in the state or UT land records.
- For this scheme a farmer family means husband, wife and minor children.
- There is no upper limit on land size; the original 2-hectare cap was dropped when the scheme was opened to all landholding farmer families.
- Eligibility is judged on land ownership recorded as on 01.02.2019; land received later by inheritance after the owner's death still counts, but land bought or gifted after that date does not make the new owner eligible.
- An Aadhaar number and a bank account seeded with Aadhaar are compulsory.
- e-KYC must be completed before payments are released.
- In some North-Eastern states and in Jharkhand, land certificates from village authorities or verified lineage records are accepted where regular land records do not exist.
Not eligible:
- Institutional landholders, and (for newly added beneficiaries) Non-Resident Indians as defined under the Income Tax Act.
- Families where any member holds or has held a constitutional post, or is or was a Union or State minister, MP, MLA, MLC, mayor of a municipal corporation or chairperson of a district panchayat.

Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
- Families where any member is a serving or retired officer or employee of the Central or State Government, a central or state PSU or a government autonomous body, or a regular employee of a local body; Multi Tasking Staff, Class IV and Group D staff are not excluded.
- Families with a retired pensioner whose monthly pension is Rs 10,000 or more (Multi Tasking Staff, Class IV and Group D pensioners are not excluded).
- Families where any member paid income tax in the last assessment year.
- Families with a practising professional registered with a professional body: doctor, engineer, lawyer, chartered accountant or architect.

National Food Security Act, 2013 - Priority Households, with Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) (NFSA / PMGKAY) — Eligibility rules

question: What are the eligibility rules for the PM POSHAN mid-day meal scheme?

Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 – Supplementary Nutrition (Poshan 2.0) — Eligibility rules

- Pregnant women, and mothers for up to 6 months after the birth.

- Anyone who qualifies can join. There is no caste, religion or income condition.
- The beneficiary must register at the nearest Anganwadi Centre with Aadhaar. A child can be registered using the mother's Aadhaar.
- Families staying in an Anganwadi area, even for a short time, can register there. A registration can be moved to the new centre through Poshan Tracker.
Not eligible:
- Food is given only to people registered at an Anganwadi Centre.
- Adolescent girls outside Aspirational Districts and the North-Eastern states (including Assam) are not covered.

Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana (NPY) — Eligibility rules
- You must be a TB (tuberculosis) patient who is notified (registered) on the Ni-kshay portal.
- Patients treated in the private sector qualify too, as long as they are notified on Ni-kshay.
- New, previously treated and drug-resistant TB patients are all covered.
- There is no age or income limit; all notified TB patients are beneficiaries.
- Children with TB are covered; if the child has no bank account, the money goes to a parent's or guardian's account.
- Patients notified on or after 1 April 2018, and those already on treatment on that date, are eligible.
Not eligible:
- A TB patient who is not notified on the Ni-kshay portal cannot receive the payment.
- Payments are only for the period the patient is on anti-TB treatment; they stop when treatment ends.

- For this scheme a farmer family means husband, wife and minor children.
- There is no upper limit on land size; the original 2-hectare cap was dropped when the scheme was opened to all landholding farmer families.
- Eligibility is judged on land ownership recorded as on 01.02.2019; land received later by inheritance after the owner's death still counts, but land bought or gifted after that date does not make the new owner eligible.
- An Aadhaar number and a bank account seeded with Aadhaar are compulsory.
- e-KYC must be completed before payments are released.
- In some North-Eastern states and in Jharkhand, land certificates from village authorities or verified lineage records are accepted where regular land records do not exist.
Not eligible:
- Institutional landholders, and (for newly added beneficiaries) Non-Resident Indians as defined under the Income Tax Act.
- Families where any member holds or has held a constitutional post, or is or was a Union or State minister, MP, MLA, MLC, mayor of a municipal corporation or chairperson of a district panchayat.

Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maan-Dhan Yojana (PM-KMY) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Small or marginal farmer who owns cultivable land of up to 2 hectares as per state or UT land records.
- Aged 18 to 40 years at the time of joining.
- Name must appear in the state or UT land records as on 01.08.2019.
- Both men and women farmers can join, in any state or union territory.
- Must agree to pay a monthly contribution of Rs 55 to Rs 200, depending on age at joining, until age 60.
Not eligible:
- Farmers already covered by another statutory social security scheme such as NPS, ESIC or an EPFO scheme.

- Institutional landholders, and present or former holders of constitutional posts, Union or State ministers, MPs, MLAs, MLCs, mayors of municipal corporations and district panchayat chairpersons.
- Serving or retired officers and employees of Central or State Government, PSUs and government autonomous bodies, and regular local body employees (Multi Tasking Staff, Class IV and Group D are not excluded).
- Anyone who paid income tax in the last assessment year.

Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maan-Dhan Yojana (PM-KMY) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
- Practising professionals registered with a professional body: doctors, engineers, lawyers, chartered accountants and architects.

Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maan-Dhan Yojana (PM-KMY) — Overview
A voluntary pension plan for small and marginal farmers (land up to 2 hectares) who join between ages 18 and 40. The farmer pays Rs 55 to Rs 200 a month, the Central Government adds the same amount, and from age 60 the farmer gets a guaranteed pension of at least Rs 3,000 a month.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare); pension fund managed by LIC.

answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) — Eligibility rules
- The applicant must be a woman who is at least 18 years old.
- No one in the household should already have an LPG connection from any oil marketing company.
- The household must fall in one of the listed groups: SC or ST households, PMAY-Gramin beneficiaries, Most Backward Classes, Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) card holders, tea and ex-tea garden tribes, forest dwellers, people living on islands or river islands, or SECC (AHL TIN) households.
- A poor household outside these groups can still qualify by giving a 14-point deprivation declaration in the set format.
- Migrant families can apply by giving a self-declaration in place of address proof and a ration card.
Not eligible:
- Households where any family member already has an LPG connection.
- Women under 18 years of age.
- Men cannot get the connection in their own name; it is issued to an adult woman of the household.

Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) — Overview
Gives adult women from poor households that have no LPG connection a deposit-free cooking gas connection. The government pays Rs 2,050 towards a 14.2 kg cylinder connection, and the first refill and the stove are also free.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.

National Food Security Act, 2013 - Priority Households, with Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) (NFSA / PMGKAY) — Eligibility rules
- The household must be identified by its State/UT government as a Priority Household (PHH) and hold an NFSA ration card.
- Each state sets its own criteria for priority households, so the rules differ from state to state.
- Nationally, up to 75% of the rural population and up to 50% of the urban population can be covered; each state has its own coverage percentage.
- The eldest woman of the household aged 18 years or more is named head of the household on the ration card; if there is no such woman, the eldest man is head until a female member turns 18.
- The Centre has told states to include eligible persons with disabilities, persons affected by leprosy and children born after 2011.
Not eligible:
- Households not identified by the state as priority households or Antyodaya households are not covered.
- Total coverage in each state is fixed using Census 2011 figures; the ceiling can be raised only after data from the next census is published.
- Ineligible, fake or duplicate ration cards, and members who have died or migrated, are removed when states verify their lists.
